title: Tip deflection of a cantilever beam under an end load
objective: how far the end of a cantilever moves under a load

equations: E' I d^2 w/dx^2 = M(x),  E' = E / (1 - nu^2)   (Euler-Bernoulli, plane strain)
delta = P L^3 / (3 E' I),  I = h^3 / 12   (tip load, one metre of depth)
sigma_max = P L (h/2) / I   (outer fibre, bending only)
assumptions: Small deflection, linear elasticity, and a beam slender enough for Euler-Bernoulli: the closed form has no shear deformation, which is why the family reports the slenderness L/h next to the answer.
The two-dimensional solver is plane strain, so the closed form compares against E / (1 - nu^2).
The root is fully clamped (both displacement components fixed) and the section is rectangular, homogeneous and isotropic.

limitations: No plasticity, no buckling, no contact and no fatigue: the answer is the elastic response to one load.
Deflections above roughly a tenth of the span are outside the linear theory this compares with.
The stress reported is the bending stress of the closed form, not the peak the solver finds at the clamp, where a real fillet and a real contact pressure change the number.
references: Timoshenko, Strength of Materials, part I, ch. 5 (cantilever with an end load, and the shear correction this closed form omits).
Boresi & Chong, Elasticity in Engineering Mechanics (plane strain replaces E with E / (1 - nu^2)).

depth.name: depth
depth.source: 1 m, the unit depth of the two-dimensional model; the load is entered as a total over it and divided by it

poisson.name: poisson
poisson.source: 0.3, the usual value for steel and aluminium alloys

ladder.name: analytic
ladder.label: Euler-Bernoulli closed form (plane strain)

ladder.name: numerical
ladder.label: immersed finite cell, plane-strain linear elasticity
ladder.method: pinneapple_simulation.immersed.solve_elasticity on a box of the section: the root face fully clamped, the tip face loaded in shear

the quantity of interest under grid refinement
